text.title: Which Rung Does This Check Belong On
text.summary: The three-question routing tree, plus the four overlays that constrain a check once it has landed. Stop at the first branch whose condition holds.

decision-tree.root-question: Can this be decided by reading the artefact's bytes — no model, no network, no reference to what a reasonable person would have wanted?

conclusion.verdict: RUNG 1. Write it as code, run it in the pre-commit hook and every CI run, 0 tokens. No exceptions for 'a model would be easier to write' — a model is never easier to maintain. Then answer the exact-vs-heuristic question below.

branch.when: decidable_from_bytes == false AND needs_real_system == true AND answer_is_mechanically_comparable == true

conclusion.verdict: RUNG 2. Write a labelled case: query in, expected ID / set / rank / boolean / count out, scored by == outside the model. The labels are the durable asset; the harness is replaceable. Runs nightly and on every prompt, corpus or model-pin change — never in the hook.

branch.when: decidable_from_bytes == false AND answer_is_mechanically_comparable == false AND would_reread_before_every_release == true

conclusion.verdict: RUNG 3. Pairwise only, formatting normalised across candidates, order swapped, disagreements recorded UNDECIDED. Report win/loss/undecided, never a mean. Count it against the declared budget of at most 15 scenarios, ever.

branch.when: decidable_from_bytes == false AND answer_is_mechanically_comparable == false AND would_reread_before_every_release == false

conclusion.verdict: RUNG H, or delete it. If you would not re-read this scenario yourself before a release, it is not important enough to pay a judge for — read it by eye, or accept the risk explicitly and say so in the record. Do not call the result deterministic.
Overlay: mark `exact: false` and set `action: flag`. A heuristic may report and must not block, however deterministic its code is.

STOP. Placement is unjustified until you can state in one line why the rung below cannot decide this. If you cannot, the check belongs one rung down — that is the common case and the whole point of the exercise.

Push it down now. A slug that does not exist becomes a rung-1 validator; a wrong item surfaced becomes a labelled rung-2 row; a vaguer tone after a prompt edit becomes a rung-3 scenario or an accepted risk. Log it in `manual_review_log` with the check id that now covers it.
Move it out of the hook. A hook that costs money and minutes per commit is disabled within a week, and then you have nothing instead of something.
